To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the aerodynamic interference between a wing and horizontal tail can cause significant flutter and/or damping reduction.

the flutter boundary for a T-tail is not a straight line, but is curved and that the flutter velocity is a strong function of the angle of incidence of the tail and the angle of attack of the main wing.
the flutter speed of the T-tail is significantly reduced by the aerodynamic interference of the tail with the wing.

the aerodynamic boundary layer effects on the flutter and damping of a flat plate.
the aerodynamic and aerodynamic effects of the boundary layer on the stability and damping of plates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the aerodynamic interference between a wing and a T-tail is a complex phenomenon which can produce flutter and/or divergence at frequencies and speeds which cannot be predicted by the simple superposition of the aerodynamic forces and moments on the wing and tail alone.
the effect of aerodynamic interference between the main wing and horizontal tail of a T-tailed configuration is to increase the flutter speed and to decrease the flutter frequency.
the aerodynamic boundary layer effects on flutter and damping of plates are very significant.

the aerodynamic interference effect is not significant for a T-tail configuration at low Mach numbers and low aspect-ratio tails.
